title: Multi-modal performance profiling of CAR T cell products
author: Schulenberg, Loeser, et al.
materials: eBioscience Foxp3/Transcription Factor Staining Buffer Set

Here we describe how to prepare single color controls for unmixing FSFC samples. In case of activation markers, stimulated cells may be used to gain appropriate signals (see stimulating cells for single-stained controls).Note: Single-stained controls should ideally be prepared using the same cell type as those analyzed with the full panel to ensure optimal spectral matching. We used freshly isolated PBMCs from healthy donors to create spectral references. The single-stained controls should exhibit strong expression of the marker of interest to ensure high signal intensities for accurate spectral definition. If the signal intensity in the single-stained control used for unmixing is lower than the full-stained sample, the signal will be extrapolated, which can result in unmixing errors. Therefore, carefully select appropriate stimulated cells for activation or exhaustion markers, and CAR T cells for detection of CAR-specific markers.Note: The use of beads as reference controls can lead to shifts in emission spectra due to differences in antibody-fluorochrome binding properties between beads and cells.7 However, modern compensation beads are optimized to reduce these discrepancies. When these limitations are considered, bead-based single-stained controls represent a faster and less labor-intensive alternative to cell-based preparations. steps.title: Obtain CAR T cell product
steps.instruction: Acquire human GD2‑C7R CAR T cell product generated by your standard activation, transduction, and expansion protocol (as previously described) or obtain PBMCs/ex‑vivo‑expanded T cells from healthy donors for controls.

steps.title: Prepare cells and activate as needed
steps.instruction: If required, stimulate cells: (i) PMA/ionomycin, (ii) CD3/CD28 beads or plate‑bound antibodies, (iii) short‑term expansion for Ki‑67, or (iv) antigen‑specific activation using LAN‑1 GD2‑positive neuroblastoma cells for GD2‑CAR T cells. For intracellular cytokine detection, add brefeldin A after 1 hour of stimulation to block secretion.

steps.title: Count cells and assess viability
steps.instruction: Adjust suspensions to ≥1 × 10⁶ viable cells per condition for the full 33‑marker panel (viability > 80 % and no clumps). For single‑color controls, prepare ≥1 × 10⁵ cells per stain.

steps.title: Prepare fixation/permeabilization reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare fixation/permeabilization solution and 1× permeabilization buffer according to the eBioscience FoxP3/Transcription Factor Staining Buffer Set (Thermo Fisher Scientific) protocol.

steps.title: Aliquot cells or beads for controls
steps.instruction: Timing: 4–5 h. Distribute cells or compensation beads into 5 mL tubes: use at least 1 × 10⁵ cells per single‑stain; for beads follow the manufacturer’s instructions (e.g., UltraComp eBeads™ Compensation Beads).

steps.title: Wash cells
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL 1× PBS, centrifuge 400 × g at 4 °C for 10 min, discard supernatant with a vacuum aspirator. For Zombie viability‑dye controls, add dye at 1:4000 dilution and PBS as needed to reach a final 100 µL staining volume.

steps.title: Block Fc receptors (optional)
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells/beads in 50 µL BD Horizon™ Brilliant Stain Buffer, add 2 µL Human TruStain FcX (Biolegend), incubate 5 min at 20–22 °C. (Fc block is optional but recommended for PBMCs.)

steps.title: Add extracellular antibodies
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of each fluorochrome‑conjugated extracellular antibody and PBS as needed to reach a final staining volume of 100 µL.

steps.title: Incubate extracellular staining
steps.instruction: Incubate at least 20 min at 4 °C in the dark (for Zombie viability‑dye controls incubate at 37 °C instead).

steps.title: Wash after extracellular stain
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL 1× PBS, centrifuge 400 × g at 4 °C for 10 min, discard supernatant, and vortex to loosen the pellet.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL fixation/permeabilization solution, vortex, and incubate 30 min at 20–22 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Wash post‑fixation
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL 1× permeabilization buffer, centrifuge 450 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant, and vortex the pellet.

steps.title: Stain intracellular markers
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of each fluorochrome‑conjugated intracellular antibody in 1× permeabilization buffer to reach 100 µL total, then incubate 30 min at 4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Final wash
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL 1× PBS, centrifuge 450 × g at 4 °C for 10 min, discard supernatant, and vortex the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend for acquisition
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 200 µL 1× permeabilization buffer and acquire on the FSFC instrument. Single‑stained controls can also be prepared in 96‑well plates using 200 µL wash volumes; an extra centrifugation step may improve pellet stability.

steps.title: Acquire full panel samples
steps.instruction: Acquire the fully stained experimental samples on the FSFC device using the same instrument settings as for the single‑stained controls.

steps.title: Unmix and inspect FSFC data
steps.instruction: Unmix raw FSFC data in SpectroFlo (Cytek) and visually confirm correct unmixing.

steps.title: Import and gate data
steps.instruction: Import FCS files into FlowJo, OMIQ, or another compatible platform and perform manual gating of single, live T cells (FSC/SSC, singlet gates, Zombie viability dye, CD3).

steps.title: Clean data (optional)
steps.instruction: Apply automated cleaning (e.g., FlowCut) if desired.

steps.title: Transform marker expression
steps.instruction: Apply an arcsinh transformation (or alternative such as biexponential) to scale marker intensities.

steps.title: Dimensionality reduction
steps.instruction: Perform UMAP (or t‑SNE) on the transformed data.

steps.title: Cluster cells
steps.instruction: Cluster the data using FlowSOM (or another clustering algorithm).

steps.title: Visualize and analyze clusters
steps.instruction: Compare cluster abundances across groups, assess relative marker expression, and optionally isolate populations by manual gating for validation.

steps.title: Integrate serial killing data
steps.instruction: Combine flow cytometry results with serial killing assay metrics (GFP‑positive area over time) to calculate percent tumor‑cell killing relative to the first time point, compute an integrated performance score, normalize data, and display results in spider charts (larger inner area indicates better functional performance).

description: Detailed characterization of therapeutic T cell products is essential for functional benchmarking in adoptive cell therapy.2,3 FSFC enables high-parameter protein-level analysis from limited sample material in a single measurement.4 By capturing large numbers of individual cellular events, FSFC provides a nuanced view of the phenotypic diversity within T cell products and supports contextualization of functional outcomes.1 The workflow was developed to characterize therapeutic T cells, with a specific focus on GD2.C7R CAR T cells.5 For this reason, markers detecting the GD2-CAR (14g2a scFv) and the C7R transgene (CD34 ectodomain) were included, which necessitates the use of GD2-positive target cells such as LAN-1. The panel incorporates markers defining T cell identity and major subsets (CD3, CD4, CD8), forming the foundation for downstream analyses. Prior to application in the CAR T cell setting, the panel was validated using peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and isolated T cells from healthy donors, which served as reference populations for optimizing staining conditions, gating strategies, and marker resolution.1 To capture differentiation and tissue-related features relevant to CAR T cell behavior, CD45RA and CCR7 classify memory states, while CD103 (tissue residency) and CXCR3 (infiltration and homing) provide information on tissue-homing potential. Additional markers assess activation (CD137, CD154, CD25, CD26, HLA-DR), effector function (IFN-γ, TNF-α), proliferation (Ki-67), and survival and susceptibility to activation-induced cell death (BCL-2, CD95), providing insight into recent stimulation, functional responsiveness, expansion potential, and cell fate after activation. Inhibitory receptors linked to T-cell regulation and exhaustion are captured by BTLA, CTLA-4, LAG-3, PD-1, TIM-3, and TIGIT. Cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-17 A, IL-22) and chemokine receptors (CCR4, CCR6) further refine assessment of functional polarization and trafficking (Table 1).
